item.title: Social Circle High School student builds bicycle rack for ice cream parlor
item.description: When Meredith Oliver started to set up her new ice cream parlor, Ida Claire, in downtown Social Circle, one of her concepts for the location was an outdoor area for families to sit and eat their frozen treats.

item.title: One arrested following interstate pursuit
item.description: An individual was arrested on Sunday night following a traffic pursuit on I-20 and a manhunt in the immediate area. According to a narrative from the Georgia State Patrol (GSP), officers attempted to stop a silver Chevrolet HHR for speeding and a tag violation on I-20 West near mile marker 92. The individual reportedly refused to stop, which led to a pursuit.

item.title: Newton splits regular season finale against Grayson
item.description: Two of the top teams in 6A basketball faced off one more time ahead of the postseason.Saturday’s iteration of the “Battle of the Rams” ended in a similar fashion to four days prior, as the Newton Lady Rams defeated the Grayson Lady Rams 59-54 to secure their 13th consecutive victory.In the boys game, Newton looked to finally get over the hump against a Grayson team that’s always seemed to have their number. Despite a hot start by Newton, Grayson charged back to score a 53-43 victory.

item.title: Local wrestlers finish season strong at state championship meet
item.description: The traditional state wrestling meets took place across the peach state this past weekend as multiple county-area athletes posted quality results.This year, all classifications in the state came together at Morrow High School for the final meet that lasted from Feb. 11-14.In total, 13 local wrestlers earned placements.

item.title: Court of Appeals upholds 2023 child molestation conviction
item.description: The Georgia Court of Appeals upheld a ruling from just under three years ago in a child molestation case.

item.title: Living Legends Gala honors five Black women educators
item.description: The Newton County Historical Committee on Black Heritage Preservation hosted its 15th Annual Living Legends Scholarship Gala on Feb. 7. This event, which aligns with Black History Month, collects donations that will be used to fund the committee’s Juneteenth scholarships awarded in the summer.

item.title: Emonie’s Closet helps clothe those in need
item.description: Emonie’s Closet is unassuming until you open its doors. Inside the black van is a rainbow of clothing that offers foster youth and families in crisis a rare gift.

item.title: Toby Davis steps away from coaching after decades in the game
item.description: Toby Davis has roamed the sidelines in Newton County and surrounding areas for decades, but the lifelong coach has decided to step away.Davis most recently served as the head coach of Alcovy High School’s flag football, soccer and softball teams.Sports have been Davis’ life, and the decision was not an easy one.

item.title: City of Covington narrowly votes to discontinue Independence Day fireworks, citing safety concerns
item.description: This Independence Day, Covington residents will have to travel beyond the Square to catch a fireworks display.

item.title: MILLIGAN: Just in time, Olympics provide new sports to fill the void
item.description: It turns out, for at least a few weeks, I’m saved from the winter doldrums after all. Just last month, I was mourning the near end of football season, officially wrapped up last Sunday night with an underwhelming Super Bowl, and wondering what sport could fill the void left by the end of seasonal pigksins action. But, lo and behold, I had forgotten the Olympics were upon us.
